scenes.title: The Subjectivity Dilemma: The Nobel-Winning Mystery
scenes.purpose: Prior to 1973, economists believed option pricing required knowing investor risk aversion and expected stock return mu
takeaways: Prior to 1973, economists believed option pricing required knowing investor risk aversion and expected stock return mu
Fischer Black, Myron Scholes, and Robert Merton discovered that dynamic delta hedging eliminates risk entirely
Their 1973 breakthrough was awarded the 1997 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Before 1973, financial economists worldwide faced an unsolved puzzle: how to determine the fair theoretical value of an option?

hi.display: Nineteen seventy-three se pehle pure world ke financial economists ke paas ek unsolved puzzle thi: option contract ki fair theoretical value kaise nikali jaye?

beats.onScreenIntent: Introduce the Nobel-winning mystery of option valuation

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Traders believed pricing required forecasting whether the stock moves up or down: the expected drift μ and investor risk preferences.

hi.display: Traders ka manna tha ki option price nikalne ke liye aapko ye predict karna hoga ki stock upar jayega ya niche, yaani stock ka expected drift mu aur investor ka risk preference.

beats.onScreenIntent: Explain why economists thought expected stock growth mu was mandatory

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: However, Fischer Black, Myron Scholes, and Robert Merton created a revolutionary proof where subjective opinions vanish completely.

hi.display: Lekin Fischer Black, Myron Scholes aur Robert Merton ne ek aisa revolutionary proof create kiya jisme investor ki subjective opinions completely gayab ho gayi.

beats.onScreenIntent: Highlight the genius of Fischer Black, Myron Scholes, and Robert Merton

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: In Chapter 15 Part 1, we derive their master differential equation step-by-step from first principles.

hi.display: Chapter Fifteen Part One mein hum unki master differential equation ko step-by-step first principles se derive karenge.

beats.onScreenIntent: Outline Part 1 roadmap: assumptions, portfolio Pi, noise eradication, and the PDE

scenes.title: The Six Governing Assumptions of the BSM Model
scenes.purpose: Asset price S follows Geometric Brownian Motion dS = mu*S*dt + sigma*S*dz with constant volatility sigma
takeaways: Asset price S follows Geometric Brownian Motion dS = mu*S*dt + sigma*S*dz with constant volatility sigma
Continuous frictionless trading with no transaction costs, no taxes, and continuous short selling permitted
Risk-free interest rate r is constant across all maturities; no arbitrage opportunities exist

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Let's first examine the six fundamental assumptions upon which the entire Black-Scholes-Merton architecture rests.

hi.display: Aaiye pehle un six fundamental assumptions ko samajhte hain jinpar Black-Scholes-Merton model ka poora architecture khada hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Present the core assumptions governing the Black-Scholes-Merton derivation

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: First: Stock price follows continuous GBM with constant volatility σ. Second: Short selling is unrestricted with full proceeds available.

hi.display: Pehla: Stock price continuous Geometric Brownian Motion follow karti hai with constant volatility sigma. Doosra: Short selling par koi restriction nahi hai aur proceeds immediately available hoti hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Explain Geometric Brownian Motion and constant volatility assumption

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Third: Zero transaction costs and taxes. Fourth: The underlying stock pays zero cash dividends during the option's lifespan.

hi.display: Teesra: Zero transaction costs aur taxes hain. Chautha: Option ki life ke dauran stock par koi dividend pay nahi hota.

beats.onScreenIntent: Clarify frictionless market conditions: zero transaction costs and short-sale freedom

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Fifth: Zero riskless arbitrage opportunities exist. And sixth: Continuous borrowing and lending at constant risk-free rate r.

hi.display: Paanchva: Market mein koi arbitrage opportunity exist nahi karti. Aur chhatva: Constant risk-free interest rate r par continuous borrowing aur lending possible hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Emphasize how ideal frictionless assumptions unlock pure mathematical replication

scenes.title: The Architecture of the Hedging Portfolio Π
scenes.purpose: Construct portfolio Pi by shorting exactly 1 derivative contract f and longing delta = (df/dS) shares of stock
takeaways: Construct portfolio Pi by shorting exactly 1 derivative contract f and longing delta = (df/dS) shares of stock
The dollar value of portfolio Pi at any instant is Pi = -f + (df/dS) * S
The short option position creates negative risk exposure that perfectly mirrors the long stock position

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: The masterstroke of the derivation is constructing a special portfolio called Portfolio Π.

hi.display: Derivation ka masterstroke hai ek special portfolio create karna jisko hum portfolio Pi kehte hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Assemble the Nobel-winning hedging portfolio Pi

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Black and Scholes defined the portfolio: short one derivative (-f), and long Delta shares of stock, where Delta = ∂f/∂S.

hi.display: Black aur Scholes ne portfolio define kiya: short one derivative position minus f, aur long delta shares of stock, jahan delta del f by del S ke barabar hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Specify the exact share quantity: delta = df/dS

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Why does this hedge work? Because an option is not an independent entity—it is derived directly from the spot price S.

hi.display: Ye hedge kyu kaam karta hai? Kyunki option contract koi independent entity nahi hai—wo stock price S ka ek derivative hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Examine portfolio value: Pi = -f + (df/dS)*S

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: When random news hits the market, both positions share the exact same Wiener shock dz, making perfect hedging possible.

hi.display: Jab market mein koi random news aati hai, toh dono positions exact same Wiener shock dz share karti hain, jisse hedging possible ho jati hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Preview the differential dPi over infinitesimal time dt

scenes.title: Expanding df via Itô's Lemma
scenes.purpose: Applying Itô's Lemma yields df = [(df/dS)*mu*S + df/dt + 0.5*(d^2f/dS^2)*sigma^2*S^2] dt + (df/dS)*sigma*S dz
takeaways: Applying Itô's Lemma yields df = [(df/dS)*mu*S + df/dt + 0.5*(d^2f/dS^2)*sigma^2*S^2] dt + (df/dS)*sigma*S dz
The stochastic shock in the derivative is strictly (df/dS) * sigma * S * dz
The drift contains expected stock drift (df/dS)*mu*S alongside theta time decay and gamma convexity

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Let's apply Chapter 14's Itô's Lemma to the change in derivative price df.

hi.display: Aaiye ab derivative contract f ke change df par Chapter Fourteen ka Itô's Lemma apply karte hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Apply Itô's Lemma to the contingent claim f(S, t)

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Because stock drift a = μS and volatility b = σS, Itô's Lemma partitions df into four distinct components.

hi.display: Kyunki stock drift a equals mu S hai aur volatility b equals sigma S hai, Itô's Lemma df ko char components mein break karta hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Identify the deterministic drift components: stock drift, theta, and gamma

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: The drift term incorporates (∂f/∂S)μS, calendar time decay ∂f/∂t, and half gamma times σ^2 S^2.

hi.display: Drift term mein del f by del S times mu S, calendar time decay del f by del t, aur half gamma times sigma square S square shamil hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Isolate the stochastic diffusion term: (df/dS) * sigma * S * dz

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: And the stochastic diffusion term simply becomes (∂f/∂S)σS*dz.

hi.display: Aur stochastic diffusion term seedha del f by del S times sigma S dz ban jata hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Set the stage for substitution into portfolio change dPi

scenes.title: The Miracle of Cancellation: Eradicating Market Risk
scenes.purpose: In portfolio differential dPi = -df + (df/dS) dS, substitute df and dS = mu*S*dt + sigma*S*dz
takeaways: In portfolio differential dPi = -df + (df/dS) dS, substitute df and dS = mu*S*dt + sigma*S*dz
The noise term -(df/dS)*sigma*S*dz cancels +(df/dS)*sigma*S*dz identically to zero
The drift term -(df/dS)*mu*S*dt cancels +(df/dS)*mu*S*dt identically to zero: mu disappears!

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Now we arrive at the most magnificent moment of the proof: calculating the change in portfolio value dΠ.

hi.display: Ab aate hain is mathematical proof ke sabse magnificent moment par: portfolio Pi ke change d Pi ko calculate karna.

beats.onScreenIntent: Formulate the portfolio differential: dPi = -df + (df/dS) dS

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: dΠ = -df + (∂f/∂S)dS. When we substitute the full expressions for df and dS, a mathematical miracle occurs.

hi.display: d Pi barabar hai minus df plus del f by del S times dS. Jab hum df aur dS dono ki full equations substitute karte hain, toh ek mathematical miracle hota hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Show the cancellation of Brownian motion dz: noise vanishes to zero

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Notice the option's shock -(∂f/∂S)σS*dz cancels against the stock's hedge +(∂f/∂S)σS*dz to exactly zero!

hi.display: Notice kijiye ki option ka stochastic shock term minus del f by del S sigma S dz stock ke hedge term se cancel hokar exactly zero ho jata hai!

beats.onScreenIntent: Show the miraculous cancellation of drift mu: subjective expected return disappears

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: And simultaneously, subjective stock drift μS*dt also cancels completely! The portfolio has zero random shock remaining.

hi.display: Aur saath hi saath subjective stock drift mu S dt bhi completely cancel ho jata hai! Portfolio mein zero random shock bachta hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: State the resulting deterministic differential: dPi has zero risk and zero variance

scenes.title: The No-Arbitrage Law: Earning the Risk-Free Rate
scenes.purpose: Because dPi contains no dz, it is completely risk-free and carries zero variance
takeaways: Because dPi contains no dz, it is completely risk-free and carries zero variance
If dPi earned more than risk-free rate r, arbitrageurs would borrow at r and buy Pi, earning free riskless profit
If dPi earned less than r, arbitrageurs would short Pi and invest in riskless bonds

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Because portfolio Π contains zero random shock dz, its return over infinitesimal interval dt is perfectly riskless.

hi.display: Kyunki portfolio Pi mein koi random shock dz nahi hai, iska return infinitesimal interval dt mein perfectly riskless hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: State the iron law of finance: riskless portfolios must earn the risk-free rate r

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: The No-Arbitrage Principle states that if a portfolio carries zero risk, it must earn exactly the risk-free rate r.

hi.display: Finance ka No-Arbitrage Principle kehta hai ki agar kisi portfolio mein zero risk hai, toh usko exactly risk-free interest rate r earn karna hoga.

beats.onScreenIntent: Formulate the arbitrage proof if dPi exceeded r * Pi * dt

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: If it earned more than r, arbitrageurs would borrow at r, buy Π, and lock in free riskless profits.

hi.display: Agar ye r se zyaada return de, toh traders risk-free rate par borrow karke is portfolio ko kharidenge aur free profit kamayenge.

beats.onScreenIntent: Formulate the reverse arbitrage proof if dPi fell below r * Pi * dt

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Therefore, dΠ must definitively equal r*Π*dt, which is r[-f + (∂f/∂S)S]dt.

hi.display: Isliye d Pi ko definitely r times Pi times dt ke barabar hona padega, yaani r times minus f plus del f by del S times S.

beats.onScreenIntent: Equate expressions: -[df/dt + 0.5*sigma^2*S^2*d2f/dS2] dt = r * [-f + (df/dS)*S] dt

left.heading: If dPi > r * Pi * dt (Free Money)
points: Because dPi contains no dz, it is completely risk-free and carries zero variance
If dPi earned more than risk-free rate r, arbitrageurs would borrow at r and buy Pi, earning free riskless profit

right.heading: If dPi < r * Pi * dt (Reverse Arbitrage)
points: If dPi earned more than risk-free rate r, arbitrageurs would borrow at r and buy Pi, earning free riskless profit
If dPi earned less than r, arbitrageurs would short Pi and invest in riskless bonds

verdict.text: Because dPi contains no dz, it is completely risk-free and carries zero variance

scenes.title: The Black-Scholes-Merton Partial Differential Equation
takeaways: Rearranging yields: df/dt + r*S*(df/dS) + 0.5*sigma^2*S^2*(d^2f/dS^2) = r*f
This parabolic PDE governs the price of ANY contingent claim dependent on underlying stock S
It combines Theta time decay, Delta underlying growth, and Gamma volatility convexity

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Let's equate both expressions and rearrange terms.

hi.display: Aaiye ab dono expressions ko equate karte hain aur terms ko rearrange karte hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Present the canonical Black-Scholes-Merton Partial Differential Equation

beats.speaker: mentor

hi.display: Minus del f by del t minus half gamma sigma square S square barabar hai minus r f plus r S del f by del S ke.

beats.onScreenIntent: Dissect each of the three left-hand terms: Theta, Delta, and Gamma

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Bringing all terms to one side yields the most famous equation in modern financial history: the Black-Scholes-Merton PDE.

hi.display: Sabhi terms ko ek side par laane par humein milti hai modern history ki sabse famous financial equation: Black-Scholes-Merton Partial Differential Equation.

beats.onScreenIntent: Explain right-hand side r*f: the required opportunity cost of option capital

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: ∂f/∂t + rS(∂f/∂S) + 0.5*σ^2*S^2*(∂^2f/∂S^2) = rf. This equation applies universally to every derivative contract.

hi.display: del f by del t plus r S del f by del S plus half sigma square S square del two f by del S square equals r f. Ye equation har derivative par universally apply hoti hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Highlight universal universality: the PDE applies to ALL derivative contracts

scenes.title: The Vanishing Mu: Why Investor Beliefs Don't Matter
scenes.purpose: Expected stock return mu does not enter the BSM PDE; only volatility sigma matters
takeaways: Expected stock return mu does not enter the BSM PDE; only volatility sigma matters
Two investors with wildly different views on stock direction (bullish vs bearish) agree on option fair value
Option pricing is governed by the cost of replication, not subjective directional forecasting

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Look at the most shocking and revolutionary feature of this equation: parameter μ does not exist anywhere!

hi.display: Is equation ka sabse shocking aur revolutionary feature dekhiye: yahan parameter mu bilkul exist nahi karta!

beats.onScreenIntent: Draw attention to the most astonishing feature of the PDE: mu is completely missing

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: This means call option fair value is completely independent of whether the stock rises or falls, or whether sentiment is bullish or bearish.

hi.display: Iska matlab hai ki call option ki fair value is baat par bilkul depend nahi karti ki stock future mein upar jayega ya niche, ya market bullish hai ya bearish.

beats.onScreenIntent: Explain why bull and bear traders agree on option price: identical replication cost

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: An ultra-bullish trader and an ultra-bearish trader are mathematically bound to agree on the exact same option price.

hi.display: Ek ultra-bullish trader aur ek ultra-bearish trader dono exact same option price par agree karne ke liye mathematically bound hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Contrast stock forecasting (estimating mu) with option pricing (estimating sigma)

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: This unlocks Risk-Neutral Valuation: we can price derivatives assuming a risk-neutral world where asset growth is r and discount rate is r.

hi.display: Yahi se Risk-Neutral Valuation principle nikalta hai: hum derivative ko aise evaluate kar sakte hain jaise market risk-neutral ho, stock growth r ho, aur discount rate bhi r ho.

beats.onScreenIntent: Conclude: the absence of mu is the birth certificate of continuous risk-neutral pricing

scenes.title: Boundary Conditions: Calls, Puts & Binary Contracts
scenes.purpose: The BSM PDE has infinite possible solutions; specific derivative prices are pinned down by boundary conditions
takeaways: The BSM PDE has infinite possible solutions; specific derivative prices are pinned down by boundary conditions
European Call boundary: f(S, T) = max(S - K, 0); European Put boundary: f(S, T) = max(K - S, 0)
Spatial boundaries: as S -> 0, call c -> 0; as S -> infinity, call c -> S - K*exp(-r(T-t))

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: The Black-Scholes-Merton PDE is a general equation with infinitely many possible solutions.

hi.display: Black-Scholes-Merton PDE ek general equation hai jiske infinitely many solutions ho sakte hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Explain why boundary conditions are needed to isolate specific option prices

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Whether you get a Call option, Put option, or Forward contract depends entirely on the contract's boundary conditions.

hi.display: Aapko call option milega, put option milega, ya forward contract milega—ye is baat par depend karta hai ki contract ki boundary conditions kya hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Specify terminal payoff boundary condition for European calls and puts at t=T

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: For a European Call, the boundary condition at maturity T is f(S, T) = max(S - K, 0).

hi.display: European call ke liye expiry par boundary condition f of S and T barabar hoti hai maximum of S minus K comma zero.

beats.onScreenIntent: Examine spatial boundary condition at S = 0: bankruptcy absorbing state

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Substituting these exact boundary conditions into the PDE allows us to derive the famous Black-Scholes formulas in Part 2.

hi.display: Inhi boundary conditions ko PDE mein substitute karke agle part mein hum famous Black-Scholes formulas derive karenge.

beats.onScreenIntent: Examine spatial boundary condition as S approaches infinity: deep ITM call behaves like forward

scenes.title: Active Recall Scenario: BSM PDE Verification for Underlying Stock & Cash Bond
scenes.purpose: For f = S: df/dt = 0, df/dS = 1, d^2f/dS^2 = 0; Left side: 0 + r*S(1) + 0 = r*S; Right side: r*S. Verified!
takeaways: For f = S: df/dt = 0, df/dS = 1, d^2f/dS^2 = 0; Left side: 0 + r*S(1) + 0 = r*S; Right side: r*S. Verified!
For cash bond f = exp(rt): df/dt = r*exp(rt), df/dS = 0, d^2f/dS^2 = 0; Left side: r*exp(rt); Right side: r*exp(rt). Verified!
Proves that underlying assets and risk-free cash bonds are simply trivial special cases of the BSM PDE

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Let's test your active recall understanding with a deep mathematical verification exercise.

hi.display: Aaiye ab aapki active recall understanding ko test karte hain ek deep mathematical verification ke zariye.

beats.onScreenIntent: Present conceptual verification challenge: does stock f = S satisfy the PDE?

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: If we treat the underlying stock itself as a derivative (f = S), does it satisfy the BSM PDE? Carefully evaluate the partial derivatives.

hi.display: Agar hum underlying stock ko hi ek derivative maan lein, yaani f equals S, toh kya ye Black-Scholes-Merton PDE ko satisfy karega? Dhyan se partial derivatives evaluate kijiye.

beats.onScreenIntent: Calculate derivatives for f = S: df/dt = 0, df/dS = 1, d^2f/dS^2 = 0

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Take a moment to substitute f = S and its partial derivatives into the Black-Scholes-Merton PDE.

hi.display: f = S aur uske partial derivatives ko Black-Scholes-Merton PDE mein substitute karke dekhiye.

beats.onScreenIntent: Substitute into left-hand side: r*S*1 = r*S

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: The correct answer is Option A. The stock's time derivative is 0, delta is 1, and gamma is 0.

hi.display: Sahi answer Option A hai. Stock ka time derivative zero hai, delta del f by del S one hai, aur gamma second derivative zero hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Compare with right-hand side r*f = r*S: exact mathematical identity

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Substituting gives 0 + rS(1) + 0 = rS, which identically equals rf! This proves the PDE is completely consistent with the underlying stock.

hi.display: PDE mein substitute karne par: zero plus r S times one plus zero barabar r S banta hai, jo exactly right-hand side r f ke barabar hai! Ye prove karta hai ki BSM PDE underlying asset ke sath perfectly consistent hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Reinforce universal consistency: underlying stock and cash bonds obey BSM PDE

data.question: Does the underlying stock itself (f = S) satisfy the Black-Scholes-Merton PDE: df/dt + r*S*(df/dS) + 0.5*sigma^2*S^2*(d^2f/dS^2) = r*f?
options: The equilibrium condition holds via continuous risk-neutral replication.
Expected asset drift determines contingent claim value directly.
Arbitrage bounds can be systematically violated in liquid markets.
Discrete binomial tree steps eliminate all underlying price variance.
data.explanation: Evaluating partial derivatives for f = S: df/dt = 0 (no time decay), df/dS = 1 (delta is 1), and d^2f/dS^2 = 0 (gamma is 0). Substituting into the PDE: 0 + r*S*(1) + 0 = r*S, which identically equals r*f = r*S. The stock satisfies the PDE unconditionally!

scenes.title: Institutional Production PDE Solvers on Wall Street
scenes.purpose: While closed-form formulas exist for vanilla European options, exotic and American options require numerical PDE solvers
takeaways: While closed-form formulas exist for vanilla European options, exotic and American options require numerical PDE solvers
The Crank-Nicolson implicit-explicit finite difference scheme discretizes S and t onto a computational grid
Tridiagonal matrix algorithms solve the PDE grid with unconditional numerical stability and O(dt^2 + dS^2) accuracy

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: On trading desks, the BSM PDE is used not just for textbook formulas, but to power billion-dollar exotic pricing engines.

hi.display: Trading desks par Black-Scholes-Merton PDE sirf textbook formula nikalne ke liye nahi, balki billion-dollar exotic pricing systems ko chalane ke liye use hoti hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Examine industrial Wall Street applications: numerical PDE solvers for exotic options

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: When options are American or have barrier features, closed-form analytical formulas do not exist.

hi.display: Jab options American hote hain ya barrier features hote hain, toh closed-form formulas exist nahi karte.

beats.onScreenIntent: Introduce the Crank-Nicolson finite difference grid architecture

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Investment banks deploy finite difference algorithms like Crank-Nicolson to solve this PDE numerically across price-time grids.

hi.display: Investment banks finite difference algorithms jaise Crank-Nicolson method use karke is PDE ko continuous price-time grid par numerically solve karti hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Explain tridiagonal matrix execution in production C++ and GPU environments

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Furthermore, Dupire local volatility models generalize this exact PDE to perfectly match real-world market volatility surfaces.

hi.display: Iske alawa Dupire local volatility models bhi isi differential equation ko generalize karke real-world volatility surfaces ko perfectly replicate karte hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Bridge to Part 2: closed-form analytical solution of the BSM PDE for European options

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Let's summarize the four foundational pillars of Chapter 15 Part 1.

hi.display: Aaiye Chapter Fifteen Part One ke chaar foundational pillars ko summarize karte hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Synthesize the historical triumph of the Black-Scholes-Merton PDE

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Pillar 1: Hedging Portfolio. Short 1 option and long Delta shares perfectly cancel out both Wiener shocks.

hi.display: Pillar One: Hedging Portfolio. Short one option aur long delta shares of stock dono positions ke Wiener shocks ko perfectly cancel karte hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Review Rules 1 and 2: market assumptions and delta-neutral portfolio architecture

beats.speaker: mentor
